newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico exports egg powder lot to United States.
newsitem.headline: Mexico exports egg powder lot to United States.

text.p: Mexico's Grupo Vitep exported in December the first lot of egg powder to the U.S. in many years, the chairman of the company based here in western Mexico said Tuesday.
"It is practically the first export lot of processed Mexican eggs to the United States," Cesar de Anda Molina, the chairman of the closely held agroindustrial group told Reuters.

"We are talking about 100 tonnes of egg powder, which is the equivalent of 500 tonnes of fresh eggs," he said, adding another achievement of the company last year was the total subsitution of egg powder imports by Mexican processed product.

"The first thing we did in 1996 was to substitute imports which had reached the total of 400,000 22-kg boxes of processed eggs," he said. The imports are subject to quotas under the North Americanm Free Trade Agreement.
De Anda Molina added he hoped exports would continue in 1997 but not only to the United States. He also viewed export possibilities to Japon, Korea, Taiwan and China.

Grupo Vitep, based in the town of Tepatitlan in the northern part of Jalisco state where Guadalajara is the capital, is the only Mexican group producing egg powder. De Anda Molina stressed fresh egg imports continued last year as opposed to egg powder.
"In price, we are offering product a little bit below others, we are competitive in comparision with Brazil, the Netherlands, Belgium, the main egg processors and export nations," he added.
He said the competitive advantage of Mexico was last year in grains prices and materials, such as fertilizers, because they were on avergae lower than in Europe.

Vitep is in a genetic production association with the U.S. company Nyline. Vitep has capacity to produce 90,000 boxes per month. "We feel that in the next three years, Mexico could become the top exporter to the United States," he said. ((--Monica Ballesca, Guadalajara bureau +523 817-0397))
